content:
Hello, I'm trying to move messages between topics and getting a strange error: Failed: Nothing to change.

The destination topic exists and is in the same channel, and in case it matters- the new topic's name is the old topic's name prefixed with [X] .
Just to check, is it possible someone else moved those messages right around the same time?

Hmm looking at it now that might be the case- is it possible that moving 3 messages would take a long long time (i.e. multiple days)?
The destination topic is #mathlib4 > [X] Variable-coefficient Grönwall inequality, integral form, and as you can see it has 3 messages that were moved. But when I posted this issue, only the first message was moved to the new thread, and I was trying to move the other 2 to it. And I tried again a couple of days after posting this. Is it possible that the initial move was of all 3 messages, but somehow only the first message moved and the rest followed it only a few days later?

Alya Abbott said:

Hmm, that would be very surprising.

This is happening again, can you take a look please? (I assume it'll auto-fix itself in a few days like the previous case)
Old: #general > theorums.fun - bounty platform for Lean theorems
New: #general > theorems.fun - bounty platform for Lean theorems
The difference is a typo in the first word. For me both links currently lead to the old topic, which is funny.
This is the list of messages by the author of the thread, which shows that there are clearly two threads right now:
Attempting to move the rest of the messages from the old topic to the new topic gives the error "Nothing to change"
I suspect this is the same sort of message-caching bug as #Zulip meta > Error moving messages: Nothing to change

Alex Vandiver said:

I suspect this is the same sort of message-caching bug as #Zulip meta > Error moving messages: Nothing to change

That's a link to the current topic, did you mean to link somewhere else?

Snir Broshi said:

(I assume it'll auto-fix itself in a few days like the previous case)

btw it auto-fixed itself, seems faster than last time
Oh, sorry, I meant #Zulip meta > Error editing message: Message was edited by another client.
Especially if it's auto-resolving in a day or two, that strongly points to bad data falling out of cache.
https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/transaction.2Eatomic/near/2470563 for where I point to the outstanding work that will resolve it.
